title: OAuth completes when the browser and the backend are on different machines
contract: apps/desktop/electron/mcp-oauth-callback-ipc.ts + the new mcp.servers.oauth.callback JSON-RPC method. title: Canonical data survives a corrupt derived index, and there is a documented offline repair
contract: docs/state-db-recovery.md states the contract: sessions and messages are CANONICAL; the full-text index and its sync triggers are DERIVED and may be detached temporarily. On an FTS corruption error class, SessionDB records a durable fts_stale marker, removes the sync triggers in the same transaction, retries canonical writes without the derived sinks, and serves searches from canonical rows through a LIKE fallback — the failing LIVE operation never runs FTS5('rebuild'), because that turned a single message write into an unbounded full-transcript rebuild. governance: Privileged where it touches the audit chain (agents/core/security/audit.py): a repair must preserve and re-verify the Merkle chain, never silently re-write rows, and a repair itself should be an owner-approved irreversible action.
